words: لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the People of the Book thought Hell extended forty years and that their punishment would last only the days named in the Torah; after those days, eternal punishment remained.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: في قوله: " وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the verse concerns some of the seventy men Moses chose: after hearing God, they misrepresented His words to their people as making obedience optional.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: نزلت في السبعين الذين اختارهم موسى ليذهبوا معه إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators instead say the verse concerns those who altered the stoning verse and Muhammad’s description.
rows.anchor: وعند أكثر المفسرين: نزلت الآية في الذين غيروا آية الرجم وصفة محمد

words: وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Jews of Khaybar invoked the promised unlettered Prophet when fighting Ghatafan and won; after Muhammad’s mission they disbelieved in him, so the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس كانت يهود خيبر تقاتل غطفان، فكلما التقوا هزمت يهود خيبر

words: وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Arabs had harmed the Jews, who found Muhammad’s description in the Torah and asked God to send him to fight the Arabs; they then rejected him out of envy and claimed prophets should be Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: كانت العرب تمر بيهود فيلقون منهم أذى، وكانت اليهود تجد نعت محمد في التوراة

words: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب
rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say the verse was revealed after allied Jews told Muslims who invited them to follow Muhammad that their current religion was no worse and they wished the invitation were to something better.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن المسلمين كانوا إذا قالوا لحلفائهم من اليهود: آمنوا بمحمد

words: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها
rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that polytheists accused Muhammad of contradicting himself by issuing and then reversing commands, and called the Quran his own contradictory speech; this verse and 16:101 answered them.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن المشركين قالوا: أترون إلى محمد يأمر أصحابه، بأمر ثم ينهاهم عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya and a group of Quraysh asked Muhammad to turn al-Safa into gold, expand Mecca, and make rivers flow there, promising to believe if he did so.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الله بن أبي أمية ورهط من قريش

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that Jews and polytheists demanded extraordinary proof: a whole heavenly book like Moses’s, a personal letter from God to Ibn Abi Umayya, or God and the angels appearing before them.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: إن اليهود وغيرهم من المشركين تمنعوا على رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report through Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about the elderly, wealthy Amr ibn al-Jamuh asking what and for whom he should give charity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح: نزلت في عمرو بن الجموح الأنصاري

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ata says a man asked how to distribute his money; the Prophet successively directed him to spend on himself, family, servant, parents, relatives, and finally God’s cause, the last being best.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: نزلت الآية في رجل أتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr reports that a force led by Abdullah ibn Jahsh killed Amr ibn al-Hadrami and seized his caravan at Nakhla on a day still within the sacred month; Quraysh protested to Muhammad, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports that Umar, Muadh ibn Jabal, and some Ansar asked Muhammad for guidance about wine and gambling, saying both impair reason and consume wealth.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل ونفر من الأنصار أتوا رسول الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says that after the warning about consuming orphans’ property, caregivers separated the children’s wealth from their own, and the verse allowing beneficial mixing was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سالم الأفطس، عن سعيد بن جبير قال: لما نزلت: {إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that caregivers separated orphans’ food and drink after the warnings in 6:152 and 4:10; leftovers spoiled, so they asked Muhammad and were told that mixing was acceptable when it served the orphans’ welfare.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: لما أنزل الله - عز وجل - {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن}

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the verse was revealed about Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi, who sought the Prophet’s permission concerning a woman called Anaq; the excerpt breaks off before his request is completed.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قال: نزلت في أبي مرثد الغنوي، استأذن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في عناق أن

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say the verse concerns Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad, although it was written in their scriptures.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: نزلت في اليهود حين كتموا صفة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ولم يبينوها للناس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Jews were miserly in affirming the person whose description and traits were in their scripture.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هم اليهود بخلوا أن يصدقوا من أتاهم صفة محمد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the three verses ending with “All-Knowing” were revealed concerning the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الآيات الثلاث إلى قوله: {عليما} نزلت في اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd instead say a group of Jews urged Ansar men not to spend their money for fear of poverty, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن زيد: نزلت في جماعة من اليهود كانوا يأتون رجالا من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about companions who drank wine and came to prayer intoxicated, unsure how many cycles they were praying or what they were saying.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أناس من أصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كانوا يشربون الخمر ويحضرون الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reports that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted companions who ate and drank; at Maghrib one led prayer and garbled the recitation of al-Kafirun, occasioning the verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن قال: صنع عبد الرحمن بن عوف طعاما ودعا أناسا من أصحاب رسول الله

words: فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا۟ مَآءًۭ فَتَيَمَّمُوا۟ صَعِيدًۭا طَيِّبًۭا
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that when her necklace was lost on a journey, Muhammad and the party stopped without water; after dawn he received the tayammum verse. Usayd ibn Hudayr called it another blessing for Abu Bakr’s family, and the necklace was found under the camel. Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmit this report.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن أبيه، عن عائشة أنها قالت: خرجنا مع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في بعض أسفاره

words: فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا۟ مَآءًۭ فَتَيَمَّمُوا۟ صَعِيدًۭا طَيِّبًۭا
rows.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
rows.claim: Ammar ibn Yasir reports that during a stay at Dhat al-Jaysh, Aisha’s Dufar-bead necklace was lost and the party waited without water until dawn; God revealed purification with clean earth, and the Muslims wiped their faces and hands up to the shoulders and armpits.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن عمار بن ياسر قال: عرس رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بذات الجيش ومعه عائشة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says he was told that Abu Bakr called Aisha blessed after the tayammum revelation.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري: وبلغنا أن أبا بكر قال لعائشة: والله إنك ما علمت لمباركة

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jews came to Muhammad with their children and asked whether the children bore sin; when he said no, they claimed they too were like them, with each day’s sins erased by night and each night’s by day. This was their self-purification.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في رجال من اليهود أتوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بأطفالهم وقالوا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah reports that Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf asked Quraysh to compare themselves with Muhammad; after Quraysh listed their virtues and old religion, the Jews called them better guided. The passage links the revelation through 4:52.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: جاء حيي بن أخطب وكعب بن الأشرف إلى أهل مكة فقالوا لهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that after Uhud Kaʿb led seventy Jews to ally with Quraysh against Muhammad; to prove sincerity they prostrated to idols, then pledged at the Kaaba to fight him, prompting these verses.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: خرج كعب بن الأشرف في سبعين راكبا من اليهود إلى مكة بعد وقعة أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported sermon, Muhammad rejects ascetic renunciation: Islam does not require abandoning meat, women, or ordinary life; the community’s monastic practice is fasting and jihad.
rows.anchor: ما بال أقوام حرموا النساء والطعام والطيب والنوم وشهوات الدنيا

words: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people asked what to do about the oaths they had sworn while agreeing to renounce things, this verse was revealed concerning those oaths.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم}

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas reports that before wine was prohibited he drank with a group of Muhajirun and Ansar, argued that the Muhajirun were better, and was struck on the nose with a jawbone; he told Muhammad, and the verse was revealed. Muslim transmits the report.
rows.anchor: حدثني مصعب بن سعد بن أبي وقاص، عن أبيه قال: أتيت على نفر من المهاجرين

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar repeatedly prayed for a clear ruling on wine: 2:219 came first, then 4:43 restricted prayer while drunk, and finally 5:90 came; when he heard “Will you then desist?” he answered that they had desisted.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة، عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the enlivened person as Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib and the one in darkness as Abu Jahl: after Hamza learned that Abu Jahl had abused Muhammad, he confronted him and embraced Islam, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأبا جهل، وذلك أن أبا جهل رمى رسول الله

words: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُۥ نُورًۭا يَمْشِى بِهِۦ فِى ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the person given light as Umar ibn al-Khattab and the person remaining in darkness as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله - عز وجل - {أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا

words: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُوا۟
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse was revealed because people behind Muhammad raised their voices during prayer.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة في هذه الآية: {وإذا قرئ القرآن} قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات وهم خلف رسول الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says people spoke during prayer when it was first prescribed, even asking one another how many cycles they had prayed; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانوا يتكلمون في صلاتهم في أول ما فرضت، كان الرجل يجيء فيقول لصاحبه

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says the verse was revealed about an Ansari youth who recited along whenever Muhammad recited.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: نزلت في فتى من الأنصار كان رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام كلما قرأ شيئا قرأ هو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the companions recited aloud behind Muhammad in obligatory prayer and confused him, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قرأ في الصلاة المكتوبة، وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وجماعة
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata, Amr ibn Dinar, and others say the verse concerns listening silently to the imam during the Friday sermon.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وجماعة: نزلت في الإنصات للإمام في الخطبة يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Abu Jahl and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith called Muhammad wretched for leaving their religion, referring to his long worship and strenuous devotion; the verse answered them.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال أبو جهل، والنضر بن الحارث للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that when Muhammad and his companions stood to pray after the Quran came down, Quraysh said it had been revealed only to make him suffer; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك قال: لما نزل القرآن على النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قام هو وأصحابه فصلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the explanation transmitted from al-Dahhak, “Ṭā Hā” means “O man.”
rows.anchor: {طه} يقول: يا رجل {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى}

words: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم
rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports that Muhammad sought a food loan from a Jewish seller for a guest, but the seller required armor as collateral; the verse consoled him about worldly goods.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع مولى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن ضيفا نزل برسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فدعاني

words: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas introduces 21:101 as an ayah people do not ask him about, then reports that Quraysh were troubled by 21:98; Ibn al-Zibaʿra asked whether it applied to all objects of worship, and Muhammad answered that it did.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: آية لا يسألني الناس عنها، لا أدري أعرفوها فلم يسألوا عنها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the commentators unanimously held that 28:56 was revealed about Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: أبا إسحاق الزجاج يقول في هذه الآية: أجمع المفسرون أنها نزلت في أبي طالب

words: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Harith ibn Uthman ibn Nawfal, who told Muhammad that he knew the guidance was true but feared the Arabs would seize them from their land because they were united against them.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الحارث بن عثمان بن نوفل بن عبد مناف، وذلك أنه قال للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

words: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about Ali, Hamza, and Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في هذه الآية قال: نزلت في علي وحمزة وأبي جهل

words: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about Ammar and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في عمار والوليد بن المغيرة

words: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported view says it was revealed about Muhammad and Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبي جهل
